name: Func_08028c04

evidence.method: families transplant (template main:080b1a14 / select_party_member.c, score 7535bp) seeded an m2c control-flow recovery over the complete symbolized owner, cross-checked against six already-exact sibling menu owners (ui_owner_7/12/24/28/30/34/38.c and menu/select_resource.c, menu/draw_mode_label.c) that share every callee here

notes: This owner is a mode-dependent 'open a resource-select menu with 2 or 3 windows' setup, not the family template's for(;;) input loop -- it has no polling loop of its own at all. Its opening/closing idiom (Func_080284dc -> Menu_AppendResourceEntry x2/x3 -> Func_08028808 -> ... -> Func_08028574 -> Func_0802851c) is directly evidenced by six already-adopted exact siblings under unidentified/main/ui/ (ui_owner_7/12/24/28/30/34/38.c) that share Func_080284dc, Func_08028808, Func_08028574, and Func_0802851c verbatim, and Func_080287a8 is independently confirmed there as Menu_AppendResourceEntry(s32). The 0x03001f38 state object's field 0x7C (a window handle) is independently confirmed by the already-adopted menu/draw_mode_label.c's `struct MenuModeLabelState.window` at the same offset.

The raw m2c draft (unset-register r0 param, 4-register-arg Func_080162d4/Func_0801e74c calls, 4 hardcoded sequential message-id literals 0xC77..0xC7A) scored 396 vs 368 bytes, 98 wrong instructions. Reading the raw instruction stream showed Func_080162d4 takes a 5th stack argument (a repeated literal 2, matching the 08021488 finding), and that the three trailing Func_0801e74c calls in the `mode!=0` branch compute their message ids as `msg_base+1`, `msg_base+2`, then `msg_base+=3` from one base local rather than four separate immediates, with the window-handle argument re-read from the field on the second and third calls but reused fresh from the register on the first (immediately after the store). Applying both, plus reconstructing the field-0x80 access as a persisted `s32 *win_b_field` pointer (mirrored in the m2c draft's own `var_r8_61`) instead of repeated M2C_FIELD stores, dropped the gap to 388 vs 368 bytes, 48 wrong instructions; switching the 0x96 field write from a signed `(s16)-1` to an unsigned `(u16)0xFFFF` immediate (matching the full 32-bit-constant-then-truncate load the reference emits there, the same widening lesson from 0801db70) brought it to 46.

Remaining disagreement is small and concentrated in two places: (1) the candidate's total size (388 vs 368) pushes some late PC-relative loads far enough that the compiler splits the constant pool mid-function with an extra branch around it -- a downstream symptom of the earlier byte surplus rather than an independent defect; (2) in the `mode==0` branch the reference reloads the 0xC76 message-id literal from a fresh pool word for both its Func_080041d8 and Func_0801e74c call sites even though they are numerically identical, while the candidate's compiler reuses one register for both (an unwanted constant-CSE the reference apparently does not perform there); giving that second occurrence its own named local variable to defeat the reuse made the score measurably worse (70 wrong instructions) rather than better, so that was reverted.

This reads as a genuine last-mile compiler-scheduling residual, not a remaining source-shape gap -- the call sequence, argument counts, and field layout are now cross-confirmed by independent exact siblings.
No external source, copied instruction bytes, inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, or compiler modification was used.
